audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed as Job's reply to Eliphaz: weight of grief, arrows of Shaddai, request for death, failed friendship as dry wadis, demand to teach, and insistence that anguish does not equal falsehood.

verses.restored: Job answered and said:

familiar.text: But Job answered and said,

verses.restored: If only my vexation were weighed, and my calamity lifted together on scales!

familiar.text: Oh that my grief were throughly weighed, and my calamity laid in the balances together!

verses.restored: For now it would be heavier than the sand of the seas; therefore my words have been rash.

familiar.text: For now it would be heavier than the sand of the sea: therefore my words are swallowed up.

verses.restored: For the arrows of Shaddai are in me; my spirit drinks their poison. The terrors of the Divine are arrayed against me.

familiar.text: For the arrows of the Almighty are within me, the poison whereof drinketh up my spirit: the terrors of God do set themselves in array against me.

verses.restored: Does the wild donkey bray over grass, or the ox low over its fodder?

familiar.text: Doth the wild ass bray when he hath grass? or loweth the ox over his fodder?

verses.restored: Can tasteless food be eaten without salt, or is there taste in the slime of purslane?

familiar.text: Can that which is unsavoury be eaten without salt? or is there any taste in the white of an egg?

verses.restored: My soul refuses to touch them; they are like loathsome food to me.

familiar.text: The things that my soul refused to touch are as my sorrowful meat.

verses.restored: If only my request would come, and the Divine would grant my hope:

familiar.text: Oh that I might have my request; and that God would grant me the thing that I long for!

verses.restored: that the Divine would be willing to crush me, loosen his hand, and cut me off.

familiar.text: Even that it would please God to destroy me; that he would let loose his hand, and cut me off!

verses.restored: Then it would still be my comfort; I would exult in pain that does not spare, for I have not denied the words of the Holy One.

familiar.text: Then should I yet have comfort; yea, I would harden myself in sorrow: let him not spare; for I have not concealed the words of the Holy One.

verses.restored: What is my strength, that I should wait? What is my end, that I should prolong my life?

familiar.text: What is my strength, that I should hope? and what is mine end, that I should prolong my life?

verses.restored: Is my strength the strength of stones, or is my flesh bronze?

familiar.text: Is my strength the strength of stones? or is my flesh of brass?

verses.restored: Is there any help in me, when sound wisdom has been driven from me?

familiar.text: Is not my help in me? and is wisdom driven quite from me?

verses.restored: To one who is fainting, covenant-kindness is owed by his friend, even if he forsakes the fear of Shaddai.

familiar.text: To him that is afflicted pity should be shewed from his friend; but he forsaketh the fear of the Almighty.

verses.restored: My brothers have betrayed like a wadi, like channels of wadis that pass away,

familiar.text: What time they wax warm, they vanish: when it is hot, they are consumed out of their place.

verses.restored: The paths of their way turn aside; they go up into emptiness and perish.

familiar.text: The paths of their way are turned aside; they go to nothing, and perish.

verses.restored: The caravans of Tema looked; the travelers of Sheba hoped for them.

familiar.text: The troops of Tema looked, the companies of Sheba waited for them.

verses.restored: They were ashamed because they had trusted; they came there and were humiliated.

familiar.text: They were confounded because they had hoped; they came thither, and were ashamed.

verses.restored: For now you have become nothing; you see terror and are afraid.

familiar.text: For now ye are nothing; ye see my casting down, and are afraid.

verses.restored: Did I say, Give to me, or from your wealth offer a bribe for me?

familiar.text: Did I say, Bring unto me? or, Give a reward for me of your substance?

verses.restored: Or, Deliver me from the hand of an adversary, or ransom me from the hand of ruthless ones?

familiar.text: Or, Deliver me from the enemy’s hand? or, Redeem me from the hand of the mighty?

verses.restored: Teach me, and I myself will be silent; make me understand how I have strayed.

familiar.text: Teach me, and I will hold my tongue: and cause me to understand wherein I have erred.

verses.restored: How forceful are upright words! But what does your arguing prove?

familiar.text: How forcible are right words! but what doth your arguing reprove?

verses.restored: Do you intend to reprove words, when the speeches of one in despair are wind?

familiar.text: Do ye imagine to reprove words, and the speeches of one that is desperate, which are as wind?

verses.restored: You would even cast lots over the orphan and bargain over your friend.

familiar.text: Yea, ye overwhelm the fatherless, and ye dig a pit for your friend.

verses.restored: Now please turn toward me; surely I will not lie to your face.

familiar.text: Now therefore be content, look upon me; for it is evident unto you if I lie.

verses.restored: Turn now; let there be no injustice. Turn again; my righteousness is still in it.

familiar.text: Return, I pray you, let it not be iniquity; yea, return again, my righteousness is in it.

verses.restored: Is there injustice on my tongue? Can my palate not discern calamities?
